title: U.S. newlywed intermarriage by race and ethnicity
definition: Share of newlyweds (married in the past year) whose spouse is of a different race or ethnicity. Hispanic is treated as an ethnicity that can pair with any race; non-Hispanic Whites, Blacks, and Asians are mutually exclusive race groups in Pew’s ACS analysis.
source: Pew Research Center analysis of U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) data, primarily 2014–2015 for detailed splits; 2015 for headline rates.
note: These are newlywed rates, not the stock of all currently married couples (10% of all married people were intermarried in 2015). Endogamy here is simply 100 minus the intermarriage rate for the same universe. Definitions differ from ancestry-specific ACS tables (e.g. Iranian diaspora endogamy).
